transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-20
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moran (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Maria Gomez (PulseMed VP Eng), Tom Lee (PulseMed ML Eng), Jordan Patel (PulseMed Security)

Summary: Quick walkthrough of Redwood's model catalog in the Console and API, discussing selecting open models, benchmark profiles, and compatibility matrices for PulseMed's POC. Discussed latency vs cost tradeoffs, quantization options, and private deployment considerations (VPC/on-prem). Agreed next steps: send benchmarks and schedule technical deep dive.

Topics covered: model selection, benchmark interpretation, compatibility matrices for GKE/GCP, KV cache and batching effects, quantization and accuracy impact, rollout policies (canary), security/SOC2/KMS questions.

00:00:12 Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, uh thanks for joining, I'm Alex, AE on this account. Quick intros?
00:00:20 Maria (PulseMed): Hi I'm Maria, VP Eng at PulseMed, we build the triage assistant and some chart summarization, Tom's our ML lead, Jordan handles security.
00:00:28 Tom (PulseMed): Hey, thanks. We're mainly interested in evaluation: can we run low-latency clinical summarization and also embeddings for retrieval at scale.
00:00:40 Priya (Redwood SE): Great, I'll walk through the model catalog and the benchmark pages in the Console. Note: some of the auto transcript may mangle names, so bear with me.

00:01:12 Priya: First screen, model catalog list — we show curated open models plus Redwood-verified performance profiles. On the right you can toggle by task: generation, chat, embeddings. For your use case I'd highlight two families: Llama2-70b-quant and Mistral-Redirect variants we host.
00:01:45 Maria: Quick question, when you say "verified performance profiles" what exactly is in there? latency numbers per seq len? throughput?
00:01:55 Priya: Yep, we surface median P50/P95 latency at different sequence lengths, throughput on our dedicated configs, token cost estimates, and a quality score from our eval harness comparing to curated prompts. Also compatibility notes — whether a model supports full KV cache, preferred quantization, and known kernel caveats.
00:02:22 Tom: And benchmarks — are those on our target infra? we run GKE on GCP, T4s and some A10s in prod dev cluster.
00:02:32 Priya: Benchmarks are run on Redwood clusters; in the catalog each profile includes the hardware used — e.g., A10G, H100 — and we provide a compatibility matrix that maps recommended runtimes/quantization to customer infra patterns — e.g., GKE + NVIDIA 3080/T4. We'll add a column for GCP GPU types specifically for your POC.

00:03:05 Alex: Also worth calling out model variants — when capacity's constrained we can route to lower-cost quantized variants or to upstream open models. That routing is policy-driven, and you can pin a given rollout to avoid surprises.
00:03:22 Jordan (PulseMed): From security side, we need to see KMS integrations and audit logs. How granular are logs? request-level? token-level cost breakdown?
00:03:33 Priya: We have per-request tracing and token-level cost/latency breakdown in Console. For Private deployments we support KMS/HSM and can ship audit logs to your SIEM. For hosted, we retain audit metadata per your retention setting.

00:04:10 Tom: Regarding quantization, how big is the accuracy hit when going from FP16 to 4-bit? for our summarization accuracy is important.
00:04:20 Priya: There's a tradeoff — our Optimize tool includes per-model quantization recommendations given your prompt set. For many models 4-bit PTQ gives small change on ROUGE/accuracy for summarization, but we recommend running evals on a subset. We can run a head-to-head using your prompts and return delta metrics.

00:04:55 Alex: I'll flag that as an action to run targeted benchmarks with your prompts. We generally show expected latency improvements and cost reduction percentages next to the quantization option in the catalog.

00:05:25 Priya: Switching to the compatibility matrix — this is a page in Console. It lists runtime requirements (CUDA version, driver), supported kernels, and notes about continuous batching and KV cache compatibility. For example some kernels for llama-like models don't fully support persistent KV on older drivers, which reduces speed for long-context chat.
00:06:00 Maria: Important for us — our context windows can be large for some notes, so KV cache behavior matters. If KV isn't supported efficiently that could add 30-50% latency for long docs.
00:06:15 Priya: Correct, and in those scenarios we recommend either (a) model variant with optimized KV kernels, or (b) use prefix caching strategies we can enable in the runtime. We'll show you measured delta in the benchmark spreadsheet.

00:06:45 Tom: Can you show the API call flow? how do we pick a model via API and request streaming?
00:06:50 Priya: Sure, quickly — the API takes model parameter such as "redwood/mistral-xxl-redirect" or an alias like "generation-low-latency". Streaming is via chunked responses; we support function/tool calling semantics and structured output enforcement. In the SDK you can set batching windows and preferred latency SLO.
00:07:20 Alex: For POC, we usually recommend starting with hosted to iterate fast, then move to Dedicated when you need reserved capacity. Private is available if you need VPC/on-prem and stricter controls.

00:07:45 Jordan: For Private, what's the deployment topology? do you manage the control plane? we need to keep logs inside our VPC.
00:07:52 Priya: Private supports a control plane with customer-managed networking; control plane can be in your VPC or we can provide an air-gapped on-prem bundle. Logs can be exported to your SIEM and keys to your KMS. We'll send the architecture doc.

00:08:30 Maria: Cost — can you give rough per-token numbers for the recommended models on A10 vs H100?
00:08:37 Alex: We'll send precise SKUs and pricing but rough ballpark: quantized 4-bit on A10 is much cheaper than unquantized on H100; H100 gives lower latencies at higher cost. We'll include cost per 1K tokens in the spreadsheet.

00:09:05 Priya: Now demoing the model catalog in Console — (screen share noises) — top left filters by task, then "Benchmarks" column shows P50/P95 and throughput. Clicking into a model brings up a benchmark sheet with plots, sample outputs, and an "Evaluate on your prompts" action.
00:09:40 Tom: That evaluate action — can it run against our dataset privately? We can't upload PHI to hosted evals.
00:09:50 Priya: Good catch — for PHI you can run evals in your Private deployment or we can run the eval engine in a Secure Eval runner inside your VPC. Otherwise we can do a synthetic eval with de-identified prompts. We'll note that as a security requirement.

00:10:20 Maria: About rollouts — if we change model versions how do we canary and rollback?
00:10:26 Priya: Console supports rollout policies with canary percentages, A/B testing, and automatic fallback. We also surface quality regression alerts tied to your eval prompt sets, so if a new model version drops quality beyond X% threshold we can automatically roll back.

00:11:00 Alex: Ok, quick recap of what we'll send: model catalog deck, benchmark spreadsheet with A10/H100/T4 rows, compatibility matrix for GKE/GCP, recommended model picks for summarization/embeddings, and pricing SKUs.

00:11:20 Jordan: I'll need SOC2 artifacts and details on encryption in transit + at rest. Also does Redwood support customer-managed KMS for hosted?
00:11:30 Priya: For hosted, customer-managed KMS is available for Dedicated and Private; for fully hosted there's envelope encryption and we can discuss bring-your-own-key options for enterprise. We'll attach the security pack.

00:12:05 Tom: One last thing — latency SLOs for production: we target 300ms median for short summaries (<= 256 tokens), and sub-second 95th for embeddings queries at QPS up to 150. Is that realistic?
00:12:20 Priya: For embeddings at that QPS we'd suggest Dedicated capacity with batching; embeddings throughput is high but batching behavior and GPU choice affect 95th. For generation 300ms median is tight but possible on H100s for short outputs; we'll show measured numbers for the recommended models.

00:12:55 Maria: Great. any blockers from our side? I'll get security docs to Jordan and Tom will send payloads.
00:13:05 Alex: Thanks all — we'll follow up with materials tomorrow.

(Transcript notes: occasional mis-heard words, speaker overlaps, filler 'um' and 'uh', auto-caption sometimes shows 'Mistral Redirect' as 'Mister redirect')

End of transcript.
